testName: Class B Knowledge Test #1 50 Questions • Passing Score 40

questions.question: During the vehicle inspection test, you will be asked to:

options.text: Change a tire.
Tell the examiner what you are checking and why.
Guess the weight of a load on a trailer.

questions.correctAnswerText: Tell the examiner what you are checking and why.
questions.explanation: During the vehicle inspection test, you must do a complete inspection of your vehicle. You must explain what you are checking and why.

questions.question: During a pre-trip inspection, belts should be:

options.text: Loosened.
Checked to see if they are tight.
Cleaned thoroughly.
Left alone and not checked.

questions.correctAnswerText: Checked to see if they are tight.
questions.explanation: When inspecting your vehicle, check all belts to make sure they are tight and not worn. Learn how much slack is correct for each belt.

questions.question: Do not decide when to shift gears based on:

options.text: Your engine speed (rpm).
Your vehicle speed (mph).
What the car next to you is doing.

questions.correctAnswerText: What the car next to you is doing.
questions.explanation: Shift gears based on your engine's rpm range. Shift up when your engine reaches the top of that range. You can also shift based on what speed each gear is best for, using your speedometer.

questions.question: If you must back up, it is helpful to:

options.text: Drive as fast as possible to finish quickly.
Walk your path first to check for obstacles.
Use only the passenger side mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: Walk your path first to check for obstacles.
questions.explanation: Before backing up, get out of the cab and check your path for obstacles. Back up slowly and check both mirrors.

questions.question: When loading a trailer, it is important to:

options.text: Put as little weight as possible on the axles.
Put the right amount of weight on the axles.
Not worry about how the cargo weight is spread out.

questions.correctAnswerText: Put the right amount of weight on the axles.
questions.explanation: When loading cargo, make sure each axle gets the right amount of weight—not too little and not too much. Bad loading can make steering harder, reduce traction, or damage the axles.

questions.question: During a basic vehicle control skills test, a look happens when:

options.text: A driver checks the gauges on the dashboard.
A driver checks their blind spots.
A driver gets out and walks to the back of their vehicle to check its position.

questions.correctAnswerText: A driver gets out and walks to the back of their vehicle to check its position.
questions.explanation: A driver uses a look when they open their door, leave their seat, and walk to the back of the vehicle to check where it is. During straight line backing, you can only take one look. During other exercises, you can take up to two looks.

questions.question: When checking your vehicle before a pre-trip inspection, look under it to:

options.text: See if the vehicle is on a slope.
Check for fresh fluid leaks on the ground.
See if the vehicle is in a parking spot.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check for fresh fluid leaks on the ground.
questions.explanation: When you first approach your vehicle, look at its overall condition and check if it is damaged or tilted. Look under the vehicle for fresh leaks of oil, grease, or fuel. Check around the vehicle for anything blocking your path, like people, other vehicles, or hanging wires or branches.

questions.question: An Individual Vehicle Distance Record (IVDR) does not need to include which of the following?

options.text: Where the trip started
Vehicle Identification Number
How many meals the driver ate

questions.correctAnswerText: How many meals the driver ate
questions.explanation: An Individual Vehicle Distance Record (IVDR) must include information about the distance traveled and the fuel purchased. It must have the trip's starting and ending points and the Vehicle Identification Number.

questions.question: Air brakes use ____ to work.

options.text: Compressed air
Liquid nitrogen
Carbon dioxide

questions.correctAnswerText: Compressed air
questions.explanation: Air brake systems use compressed air to make the brakes work.

questions.question: Air tank drains should:

options.text: Only be used by mechanics.
Only be used when it is wet outside.
Be used to empty the tanks completely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be used to empty the tanks completely.
questions.explanation: In an air brake system, air tank drains remove water and compressor oil from the air tanks. Always drain the tank completely when you use a drain.

questions.question: What is an example of required emergency equipment?

options.text: A spare electrical fuse.
A loud horn.
A battery-operated flashlight.

questions.correctAnswerText: A spare electrical fuse.
questions.explanation: Commercial vehicles must have emergency equipment. This includes spare fuses, reflective triangles or flares, and a fire extinguisher.

questions.question: What does cargo blocking do?

options.text: Holds the cargo in a large box
Stops cargo from sliding during transport
Prevents others from buying the cargo

questions.correctAnswerText: Stops cargo from sliding during transport
questions.explanation: Blocking and bracing prevent cargo from moving or shifting during transport.

questions.question: What determines your blood alcohol concentration (BAC)?

options.text: How much you drink
How often you drink
The temperature of the drink

questions.correctAnswerText: How much you drink
questions.explanation: Your BAC depends on how much alcohol you consume, how fast you drink it, and your body weight.

questions.question: Which is NOT an example of a distracted person that motorists should worry about?

options.text: A driver talking to a passenger in their vehicle
A person sitting on a bench waiting for a bus
A construction worker on the side of the road

questions.correctAnswerText: A person sitting on a bench waiting for a bus
questions.explanation: Be careful around distracted drivers and pedestrians. Drivers talking to passengers may not focus on the road. Workers on the road may not notice traffic because they are focused on their job.

questions.question: When changing lanes, what should you do?

options.text: Do not use your mirrors
Use your mirrors
Do not use your turn signals

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your mirrors
questions.explanation: Always use your turn signals and check your mirrors when changing lanes.

questions.question: When leaving your vehicle, what should you do?

options.text: Apply the air brakes
Apply the parking brake
Do not apply brakes if the vehicle is left out of gear

questions.correctAnswerText: Apply the parking brake
questions.explanation: Always use the parking brake when you park. You can also chock the wheels if needed.

questions.question: What usually happens to bridges?

options.text: They do not freeze
They have heaters to prevent freezing
They freeze before other road surfaces

questions.correctAnswerText: They freeze before other road surfaces
questions.explanation: Bridges freeze before other parts of the road. Drive carefully on bridges when the temperature is near freezing.

questions.question: What should dual tires do?

options.text: Always touch each other
Touch each other fairly often
Not touch each other

questions.correctAnswerText: Not touch each other
questions.explanation: When inspecting your vehicle, make sure dual tires do not touch each other or any other part of the vehicle.

questions.question: When passing parked vehicles, what should a driver do?

options.text: Stay close to the vehicles
Watch for people exiting vehicles
Flash their headlights

questions.correctAnswerText: Watch for people exiting vehicles
questions.explanation: Be careful passing parked vehicles. A person may step out of a vehicle or from between vehicles without looking. A driver may start moving before seeing you.

questions.question: During the vehicle inspection test, what will you be asked to do?

options.text: Explain why you must check the items you are checking
Change the coolant
Replace a headlight

questions.correctAnswerText: Explain why you must check the items you are checking
questions.explanation: During the vehicle inspection test, you will inspect your vehicle completely. You must explain what you are inspecting and why.

questions.question: A CMV driver with any detectable alcohol in their system but below the legal limit will:

options.text: Be taken out of service for two hours.
Be taken out of service for 10 hours.
Be taken out of service for 24 hours.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be taken out of service for 24 hours.
questions.explanation: If you have any detectable alcohol in your system while driving a CMV, even if your blood alcohol level is below 0.04 percent, you will be taken out of service for 24 hours. Driving under the influence is illegal and dangerous.

questions.question: A pre-trip inspection should include:

options.text: Checking the engine oil level.
Draining the coolant.
Washing the tire rims.

questions.correctAnswerText: Checking the engine oil level.
questions.explanation: During a pre-trip inspection of the engine, check the oil level, coolant level, and the condition of the hoses.

questions.question: Shaded areas of a road:

options.text: Usually do not freeze.
Are protected from moisture and cannot freeze.
Stay slippery after ice melts on other parts of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay slippery after ice melts on other parts of the road.
questions.explanation: Shaded areas get less sunlight and warm up slowly. They stay icy and slippery after ice has melted on other parts of the road.

questions.question: When stopping, the brake pedal should be:

options.text: Pressed down quickly with both feet.
Pressed down gradually.
Released quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pressed down gradually.
questions.explanation: When braking, press the pedal down slowly to ensure a smooth, safe stop.

questions.question: Dry bulk tanks:

options.text: Cannot be driven on interstates.
Require special care when driving.
Are usually not allowed to cross railroad tracks.

questions.correctAnswerText: Require special care when driving.
questions.explanation: Dry bulk tanks need special care because they have high centers of gravity and the load can shift during travel.

questions.question: If the coolant temperature gauge goes above the highest safe temperature, you should:

options.text: Continue driving.
Pull over and find out what is wrong.
Turn on the air conditioner.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull over and find out what is wrong.
questions.explanation: If the coolant temperature is too high, stop driving as soon as possible. There may be a serious problem that could cause engine failure or fire.

questions.question: When adjusting your mirrors before a trip:

options.text: No part of your vehicle should be visible in any mirror.
Part of your vehicle should be visible in the mirrors.
More than half of each mirror should show the vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Part of your vehicle should be visible in the mirrors.
questions.explanation: Properly adjusted mirrors should show some part of your vehicle. Seeing your own vehicle helps you judge the position of other objects on the road.

questions.question: When taking the on-road driving skills test:

options.text: You do not have to use the type of vehicle you want to be licensed to drive.
You must use the type of vehicle you want to be licensed to drive.
The type of vehicle does not matter.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must use the type of vehicle you want to be licensed to drive.
questions.explanation: You must take the on-road test in the same type of vehicle for which you want to be licensed.

questions.question: Driving with a cargo of hanging meat in a trailer:

options.text: Should be avoided during summer months.
Is difficult because animals are attracted to the meat smell.
Is challenging because the load has a high center of gravity.

questions.correctAnswerText: Is challenging because the load has a high center of gravity.
questions.explanation: Transporting hanging meat requires careful driving. The load is unstable because it has a high center of gravity and the meat can swing, making the vehicle harder to control.

questions.question: What is removed when an air tank is drained?

options.text: Water and oil
Ammonia
Liquid cleaners

questions.correctAnswerText: Water and oil
questions.explanation: Air brake system tanks have drains that remove water and compressor oil that build up over time. If water and oil accumulate, they can damage the brakes.

questions.question: Why should a driver accelerate slowly on a surface with poor traction?

options.text: Because slow acceleration is always a good practice.
To avoid losing control of the vehicle.
To avoid going faster than the vehicle ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: To avoid losing control of the vehicle.
questions.explanation: Accelerate slowly in poor traction conditions like rain or snow. This helps you maintain control of your vehicle.

questions.question: Why should a driver accelerate especially slowly when traction is poor?

options.text: Because slow acceleration is always a good practice.
To avoid losing control of the vehicle.
To avoid going faster than the vehicle ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: To avoid losing control of the vehicle.
questions.explanation: In slippery conditions, accelerate gradually. Too much power can cause you to lose control.

questions.question: What is true about distracted driving?

options.text: It is caused only by physical distractions.
Pre-programming radio stations will increase it.
It can be prevented by avoiding conversations with others while driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: It can be prevented by avoiding conversations with others while driving.
questions.explanation: Distractions can be physical (reaching for objects), mental (talking with passengers), or both (texting). You can reduce distracted driving by pre-programming your radio, planning your route ahead of time, avoiding difficult conversations while driving, adjusting mirrors before you leave, and not eating, drinking, or smoking while driving.

questions.question: Are rims with welding repairs safe to use?

options.text: No, they are not safe to use.
Yes, if used on rear tires.
Yes, if carrying a light load.

questions.correctAnswerText: No, they are not safe to use.
questions.explanation: Never use wheels or rims that have been welded. They are not safe.

questions.question: How often must drivers check that cargo is secure?

options.text: Every 10 miles.
Every 150 miles.
Every 500 miles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Every 150 miles.
questions.explanation: Check that cargo is secure within the first 50 miles of your trip. Then check again every three hours or every 150 miles.

questions.question: What should you do when traveling down a steep hill?

options.text: Use the air brakes.
Put the vehicle in a low gear and use engine braking.
Downshift repeatedly instead of using the brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Put the vehicle in a low gear and use engine braking.
questions.explanation: On long or steep downhill grades, use engine braking to control your speed. Use your brakes only as a backup.

questions.question: Where are foundation brakes used?

options.text: Only on the front wheels.
Only on the rear wheels.
On all four wheels.

questions.correctAnswerText: On all four wheels.
questions.explanation: Foundation brakes are on each wheel of a vehicle. The most common type is the s-cam drum brake.

questions.question: How often should you check your mirrors while driving?

options.text: Only when changing lanes.
Frequently.
Only if you suspect a problem.

questions.correctAnswerText: Frequently.
questions.explanation: Check your mirrors regularly while driving. This helps you stay aware of traffic and watch for problems with your vehicle.

questions.question: How much steering wheel play is acceptable?

options.text: No more than 10 degrees.
No more than 50 degrees.
No more than 75 degrees.

questions.correctAnswerText: No more than 10 degrees.
questions.explanation: Your steering wheel should have no more than 10 degrees of play, which is about two inches of movement on a 20-inch wheel. More play than this makes steering difficult.

questions.question: Why are roads especially slippery right after rain begins?

options.text: Water mixes with oil and grease on the road surface.
Tires are not made for wet weather.
Water has not yet absorbed the dirt and grease.

questions.correctAnswerText: Water mixes with oil and grease on the road surface.
questions.explanation: When rain first begins, water mixes with oil and grease already on the road. This creates a slick film before the rain washes it away.

questions.question: If you get a traffic ticket in your personal car, what must you do?

options.text: You must tell your employer.
Your CDL will not be affected.
Law enforcement will tell your employer.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must tell your employer.
questions.explanation: You must tell your employer within 30 days if you are convicted of any traffic violation while driving any vehicle. Parking violations do not count.

questions.question: A tired driver:

options.text: Is usually extra alert.
Is usually more careful than a typical driver.
May be slower to make important decisions than a typical driver.

questions.correctAnswerText: May be slower to make important decisions than a typical driver.
questions.explanation: Tired drivers are slower to see or react to dangers. They cannot make important decisions as quickly as rested drivers.

questions.question: How should you hold a steering wheel?

options.text: With one hand while the other hand rests.
With both hands to keep a firm grip.
Release it if the vehicle is approaching a bump.

questions.correctAnswerText: With both hands to keep a firm grip.
questions.explanation: Hold the steering wheel firmly with both hands on opposite sides of the wheel.

questions.question: What do header boards do?

options.text: Should never be used.
Protect the driver from cargo that shifts during a crash or emergency stop.
Protect the driver's head when entering the truck cab.

questions.correctAnswerText: Protect the driver from cargo that shifts during a crash or emergency stop.
questions.explanation: Header boards (also called "headache racks") protect the driver if cargo moves forward during a crash or emergency stop.

questions.question: Can you have more than one driver license?

options.text: Yes, if one is for business purposes.
Yes, if they are from different states.
No, you cannot have more than one license.

questions.correctAnswerText: No, you cannot have more than one license.
questions.explanation: You cannot have more than one driver license at any time. States share information through a computer system to prevent this. Breaking this rule can result in fines or jail time.

questions.question: A ____ allows a driver to slowly apply spring brakes.

options.text: Modulating control valve
Trailer air supply control
Relay valve

questions.correctAnswerText: Modulating control valve
questions.explanation: A modulating control valve lets the driver slowly apply spring brakes. A lever on the dashboard controls this valve in equipped vehicles.

questions.question: Which of these is NOT a sign of when to change gears?

options.text: Engine speed (rpm)
Road speed (mph)
The speed of the vehicle next to you

questions.correctAnswerText: The speed of the vehicle next to you
questions.explanation: There are two signs for when to shift gears: engine speed (rpm) and road speed (mph). Check your vehicle manual for the correct rpm range. Watch your speedometer and shift up as you reach higher speeds. Never use the speed of other vehicles to decide when to shift.

questions.question: What is blocking used for?

options.text: To keep cargo in a large box.
To stop cargo from sliding in a trailer.
To stop cargo from falling out of a trailer.

questions.correctAnswerText: To stop cargo from sliding in a trailer.
questions.explanation: Blocking is placed on all sides of cargo to keep it from sliding while the vehicle is moving.

questions.question: If an aggressive driver confronts you, what should you do?

options.text: Make eye contact.
Try to stay in their way.
Ignore any hand gestures.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ignore any hand gestures.
questions.explanation: The best thing to do is get out of their way if possible. Do not make eye contact, as this may make them more angry. Ignore any hand gestures they make.

questions.question: What is aggressive driving?

options.text: Driving in a selfish or pushy way.
Driving with strong care for other drivers' safety.
Driving in the left lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Driving in a selfish or pushy way.
questions.explanation: Aggressive driving is driving in a selfish, bold, or pushy way without care for the safety of other drivers.
